title: Aviation Transport Security Amendment (Inbound Cargo Security Enhancement) Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Backed the bill allowing the minister to ban certain air cargo following the 2010 Yemen printer bomb plot, with penalties of $17,000 for individuals and $34,000 for aircraft operators, and separately raised concerns about a dispute between Griffith and Dubbo councils over airport security screening fees after Rex, which flew between 60,000 and 90,000 passengers a year to Sydney, dropped its Melbourne service.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Summed up the bill as strengthening Australia's response to threats like the 29 October 2010 Yemen cargo bomb plot, recalling he was in London receiving British security briefings on the incident at the time, and confirmed no cargo ban will be imposed without consulting the foreign affairs and trade ministers.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Conroy
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Aviation Transport Security Act 2004 to allow the government to quickly prohibit or restrict inbound air cargo via disallowable instruments, with strict liability penalties of $34,000 for aircraft operators and $17,000 for other industry participants, following the 2010 Yemen incident where explosives were hidden in printers.
